prompt:
CONCEPT: a citizen of the Hydrogen Nation, of the Water House. A female personification character with a clear glass bottle of pure drinking water — a cylindrical silhouette, a cap, condensation droplets as her motif — the object reimagined as a woman in cloth and ornament that carry its materials, colors, shape and motifs. She does NOT hold, carry or wield the object; it is not a separate object. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.
ELEMENT TRAITS of Hydrogen (H) to carry in her design and the scene: airy, pale and luminous, always rising: translucent layers, upward-drifting hair and hems, a faint pale-blue flame (hydrogen burns almost invisibly), star-light and fusion white, water droplets and mist; it is the lightest element, the fuel of stars and half of every drop of water. Palette: pale sky blue, white, silver, a faint violet flame, clear glass.
HOUSE TRAITS of Water: water as it comes from the sky: cloud, rain, mist and steam — translucent layered veils, droplets as beads, a cool clear palette; the rising-and-falling side of water. Palette: clear glass, rain blue, cloud white, silver droplets.
AGE: in her twenties — smooth youthful skin, soft full cheeks; minimal facial lines (no nasolabial folds, crow's feet, under-eye bags or cheek creases) and a soft smile that never creases her face.
SILHOUETTE: slender build; long side-swept hair; clear glass-blue hair with bright highlights.
FACE (her own structure, not the style's default face): oval face; narrow upturned eyes; thin arched brows; small button nose; small bow lips; azure-blue eyes.
WORLD — STEAMPUNK: around 1900, an airship harbour: great hydrogen gas envelopes under a mooring mast, brass valves and gauges, an electrolysis laboratory with glass jars and a spectroscope, telegraph wires, dawn haze. A brass-banded glass canteen with a cork and a leather strap. COSTUME (citizen, steampunk): her object leads — its silhouette, parts and materials must read at first glance in her outfit and headpiece, the object reimagined as cloth, leather and brass fittings; the steampunk era only sets the late-Victorian cut and the brass-and-leather finish. Steam, pipes and gauges in the scene; no modern plastic, no sci-fi. LIGHT: hazy gaslight and a smoky overcast sky, unless TIME & WEATHER says otherwise.
STYLE: Polished 2.5D game key art with clean linework, controlled anime facial design, layered cel-to-soft shading and crisp costume and prop detail. Use a vivid, readable silhouette and campaign-quality lighting.
EXPOSURE (bold): her outfit opens to show skin — a deep open neckline with natural cleavage, bare shoulders or arms, a high slit or a short hem where the outfit allows; pieces stay symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Chest and pelvis covered; no corset; keep the object's shape, material and palette.
OUTPUT: one character image that works as card art. Vertical 2:3 frame, full body with head and feet inside the frame with clear margins, face turned toward the camera (front or three-quarter). Standing, card-ready pose; the environment may be rich while her design stays fully readable.
BODY: a normal human body — one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint. Hands and feet may be partly hidden by the pose or the frame.
ONE FIGURE ONLY. No second character, no living creature, no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logo, no watermark, no speech bubble, no frame border.
ANATOMY: natural adult proportions, both hands drawn correctly as hands. No extra limbs.
